name: Acne
typical_presentation: Spots such as blackheads, whiteheads, red bumps and sometimes deeper, painful lumps, mostly on the face, chest and back. Very common in teenagers and young adults.
general_guidance: Wash gently twice a day and avoid squeezing spots, which can leave scars. A pharmacist can explain over-the-counter options. See a doctor if acne is severe, painful, leaving marks or scars, or affecting how you feel.

name: Eczema
typical_presentation: Dry, itchy skin with red or darker patches that can become rough, thickened, cracked or weepy. Often in skin folds such as the inner elbows, behind the knees and on the neck. It tends to come and go in flare-ups.
general_guidance: Moisturize often, use mild soap-free cleansers and avoid things that set it off, such as harsh soaps. See a doctor if it is widespread, very itchy, weeping or crusted, or not improving, because skin infections and fungal infections can look similar.

name: Psoriasis
typical_presentation: Clearly outlined, raised patches covered with silvery or whitish scale, commonly on the elbows, knees, scalp and lower back. It is long-term and not contagious.
general_guidance: Moisturizing can ease dryness and scaling. Psoriasis needs a doctor's diagnosis and is usually managed with treatment a doctor recommends, so see a doctor, especially if patches are spreading or your joints are painful or swollen.

name: Scabies
typical_presentation: Intense itching, usually worse at night, with small bumps or short, thin lines (burrows), often between the fingers, on the wrists, around the waist and in other skin folds. People in the same household are often itchy too.
general_guidance: Scabies spreads through close skin contact and is treated with prescription medicine, so see a doctor. People you live with may need to be checked and treated at the same time.

name: Fungal skin infection (tinea or ringworm)
typical_presentation: A red or darker, ring-shaped or spreading patch with a scaly, raised edge that is often itchy. Common in hot, humid weather and in areas that stay damp, such as the groin, feet and skin folds.
general_guidance: Keep the area clean and dry. Do not put steroid creams on it unless a doctor advises, because they can make fungal infections worse. See a doctor or pharmacist if it spreads or does not improve.
